mechanism_narrative: The WORKPLACES weekly mean has crossed from +1.3 to -1.7 over four weeks, signalling that office-based commuting demand has flipped net-negative. Loss of weekday commuter footfall removes a fixed share of lunchtime and after-work retail trips, so RETAIL_REC trends lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean crosses from positive to negative (last value < 0.0 after a value > 0.0 within the prior 3 weeks)
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 1.3 -> 0.6 -> -0.3 -> -1.7 across the four snapshot weeks
regime_hint: steady state with receding office attendance
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES is negative and falling, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has declined monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-9.9, -10.1, -10.6, -11.1), a persistent always-on trend rather than noise. Because transit-station trips are a leading indicator of discretionary trip-taking, the continued erosion mechanically depresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined in each of the four snapshot weeks with no reversal
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean while TRANSIT continues its four-week monotonic decline.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has risen to +7.9, its highest value in the snapshot, indicating substitution of out-of-home time with time at home. Households that shift hours into the home cut discretionary trips to stores, so the rising residential share predicts a lower RETAIL_REC mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the prior 28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above +7.5.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is pinned near +10 while RESIDENTIAL rises. The joint pattern is a stay-home provisioning regime in which essential spend is captured by grocery channels and discretionary retail wallet share shrinks. The interaction of stable essential demand and rising home time therefore drives RETAIL_REC lower over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM held 9.6-10.4 while RESIDENTIAL climbed to 7.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days rises above its prior 14-day mean in weeks where GROCERY_PHARM stays above +9 and RESIDENTIAL above +7.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS dropped 4.8 points between the t-2w and t-1w readings, a late-summer outdoor-aversion shock. Park trips are typically chained with nearby retail stops, so a sharp park decline removes that chained demand and produces a short-lived one-week drag on RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -38.3 to -43.1 in one week
failure_condition: In the week following a PARKS week-on-week drop below -3.0 points, RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to that same week.

mechanism_narrative: A joint contraction in TRANSIT (below -11) and WORKPLACES (below -1.5) is the signature of renewed containment tightening, as transit capacity and office occupancy are the first series to fall under new advisories. Such tightening imposes capacity limits on retail venues, so the combined threshold breach predicts lower RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT < -11.0 and WORKPLACES < -1.5 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT hit -11.1 and WORKPLACES hit -1.7 in the final snapshot week
failure_condition: After a week with TRANSIT < -11.0 and WORKPLACES < -1.5, the subsequent 14-day mean RETAIL_REC is at or above the preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has been flat within a 0.7-point band for four weeks while the PARKS decline decelerated from -4.8 to +1.8 points week-on-week. Deceleration of the outdoor drag plus a flat retail floor marks the seasonal trough, so mean RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change > +1.5 points (deceleration of the decline)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -43.1 to -41.3 while RETAIL_REC held at -13.9
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the 28 days after a PARKS week-on-week improvement above +1.5 points is lower than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The snapshot sits in the late-August back-to-school window, when apparel, supplies and general-merchandise purchases rise regardless of commuting or transit drags. This calendar effect is strong enough to lift the next four-week RETAIL_REC mean above the depressed current four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:decision time point is 2022-08-15, inside the northern-hemisphere back-to-school period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean of about -13.8 during the back-to-school window.
